svg.title: RIEMANN-MASULLO-DIAGRAMS DB — Appendix B · AppB_AnalyticNT, declaration by declaration
svg.desc: riemann-masullo at 72a10ff: the 1,304 declarations of the 119 items on CB, each with its kind, file, line and state; 108 declarations with a Deviation: line, quoted; and the items of other directories each item uses.

g.text: riemann-masullo at 72a10ff: the 1,304 declarations of the 119 items on CB, each with its kind, file, line and state; 108 declarations with a Deviation: line, quoted; and the items of other directories each item uses.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Posters: M1, what the targets rest on · M2, the steps with no known repair · M3, the paper by depth · M4, every chapter · M5, the refutations. Names, items, files, entries and posters are links, underlined under the pointer: a card's title or a Lean name opens the source at the pin.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: How to read it. The expansion of CB's cards, in the same order: one block per item, its heading opening the card, and under it, in italics, the first sentence of its first declaration's docstring, quoted. Then the declarations whose docstring states how the Lean departs from the print, each with its Deviation: line quoted from the Lean

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: source (Apache-2.0), then every declaration of the item. A name opens its line at the pin. A declaration's state is read from the terms: open when it uses sorryAx, resting when something open is below it. That a declaration states what its Deviation: line says is the docstring's claim, not checked here.

g.text: The finite part is the Euler product expansion (B.4.2.5)–(B.4.2.7) integrated termwise by Mellin inversion, with the normalizations of F36 (both samples carry the centred weight q^(-m/2) log q). The archimedean part is realHeckeArchimedean_mellinLogDeriv and complexHeckeArchimedean_mellinLogDeriv applied to the centred profile x ↦ exp(-x/2) f x, whose

g.text: The scaled finite Fourier pairing defines a continuous linear functional on additive tests.

g.text: The additive character is allowed to be any translate of the standard character by a nonzero field multiplier, with the corresponding self-dual measure.

g.text: The nonzero multiplier specifies the character as in (B.4.4.12).

g.text: The zeros of the completed Hecke L-function of a unitary character lie in the closed critical strip 0 ≤ Re s ≤ 1: the Euler product does not vanish for Re s > 1, and the functional equation reflects this to Re s < 0.

g.text: An absolute constant gives a zero-free region for each finite Hecke L-function, with a scale depending on the field and character.

g.text: The scale is chosen greater than 1/3 so the logarithm in the denominator is positive at every height. It is an existential scale and may be enlarged to exclude an exceptional zero. The separate real-zero clause is false.

g.text: For each derivative order there is a nondecreasing sequence of heights tending to infinity in absolute value and growing at most linearly in the index.

'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The finite set records only finite places. All archimedean factors have already been removed from L. The supremum is expressed pointwise, and analyticity ensures the iterated derivatives are defined on the segments. The unit intervals of Theorem B.6.1.7, reflected for the conjugate character on the negative tail, give heights within one of the index for the application of §B.3.

g.text: Adds the half-endpoint correction. For c ≥ 1 the absence of a norm-one coefficient gives exponential decay to the right. The initial contour lies strictly to the right of the pole, so the estimate also holds at the pole ordinate.

text.tspan: · pp. 646–647 · 22 declarations, 1 deviating from the print

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The integral along the left edge is bounded by the cutoff to the power -δ times a cubed logarithm.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The width δ uses the maximum absolute shifted height. The estimate allows the unregularized logarithmic derivative to contribute a term of order 1 / δ near its pole. The punctured disc is the hypothesis on α in Theorem B.6.1.3. Both constants may depend on the chosen width.

g.text: On either horizontal edge the squared logarithm of its shifted height controls the integral.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Each edge uses its own absolute shifted height. The contour width uses the maximum of both heights, and the estimate starts at a sufficiently large height for the logarithmic-derivative estimate of §B.6. The punctured disc is its hypothesis on α. Both constants may depend on the width.
